extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: TextVQA is a Visual Question Answering dataset containing 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reading and reasoning about text in images to answer. Images are sourced from Open Images v3 from categories that tend to contain text (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard). Each question-image pair has 10 ground truth answers provided by humans.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach (Facebook AI Research, Georgia Institute of Technology)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from Open Images v3 dataset, selecting categories that tend to contain text. A three-stage crowdsourcing pipeline was used: (1) annotators identified images without text; (2) annotators provided 1-2 questions per image requiring reading the text; (3) 10 answers were collected per question with quality filtering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In some cases, when the system is unable to detect text we get 0 OCR tokens but those cases are restricted to 1.5k images and we manually verified that the images actually do contain text.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from Open Images v3 dataset, specifically from categories that tend to contain text (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard). Training and validation sets were collected from Open Images' training set; test set from Open Images' test set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were filtered by running Rosetta OCR on 100 random images per category to compute average OCR boxes, used as per-category sampling weights. Annotators flagged images without text; filtering those and noisy annotator data resulted in 28,408 images. Questions were removed where a majority of workers marked them as: no text in image, not a question, not requiring text reading, or unanswerable. Hand-crafted questions were used to identify and filter out bad annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage crowdsourcing pipeline: (1) annotators flagged images without text; (2) annotators provided 1-2 questions per image requiring reading text in the image, with instructions to ensure answering requires reading text; (3) 10 answers collected per question with quality flags (no text, not a question, doesn't require reading, unanswerable). Answer quality instructions similar to VQA and VizWiz datasets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% of questions, while 3 or more annotators agree on the most common answer for 97.9% of questions. Human accuracy is 85.01% on validation and 86.79% on test.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is motivated by the needs of visually impaired users, for whom up to 21% of questions to assistive devices involve reading and reasoning about text in images.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset does not have significant biases with respect to images and questions, as shown by low accuracy of question-only (8.09%) and image-only (6.29%) baselines. The most common answer ('yes') is the majority answer for only 4.71% of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: 8.9% of TextVQA questions can only be answered by combining multiple OCR tokens, which is left as future work. The OCR model fails at detecting text that is rotated, unstructured (e.g., a scribble) or partially occluded.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of VQA models that can read and reason about text in images. The dataset is split into train (34,602), validation (5,000), and test (5,734) sets.
